project.title: Separation of the Bioactive Exosomes from Extracellular Vesicles Derived from Murine CTLs
project.projectDescription: Recently, instead of ultracentrifugation, development of new preparation protocol is demanded for research of reliable bioactivity and drug discovery of extracellular vesicles (EVs). In this study, we propose a novel method for large scale preparation of high-performance extracellular vesicles focusing on membrane negative charge.
project.sampleProcessingProtocol: Exhaustive proteomic analysis of L-s and H-s CTL EVs was performed by quantitative LC-MS/MS of iTRAQ-labeled EV peptides (Intégrale Co., Ltd.). Briefly, L-s and H-s CTL EVs were digested with trypsin (AB Sciex) and labeled with iTRAQ (iTRAQ Reagent-8 Plex Kit: AB Sciex). Reporter tags 114 and 115 were used for the isolated peptides of L-s and H-s CTL EVs, respectively. The labeled samples were combined and fractionated into 6 fractions by strong cation exchange chromatography, and desalted using MonoSpin® C18 column (GL Science). Each peptide fraction was analyzed using Q Exactive Plus (Thermofisher Scientific) coupled on-line with a capillary HPLC system (EASY-nLC 1200, Thermofisher Scientific) to acquire MS/MS spectra.
project.dataProcessingProtocol: Proteome Discoverer (version 2.1, Thermo Fisher Scientific) was used to search against protein database SWISS-Prot and quantitate iTRAQ label-based quantification.
